title: Marin Alpine Trail E-bike
review: Recently bought a Marin Alpine Trail E-bike at great value - was £200 less than everywhere else. On ordering website said that it was in stock with next day dispatch. However, after 4 days I hadn't heard anything. I sent an e-mail and called repeatedly with no response. After being on hold for 35mins, I managed to get through on the phone and the customer service was professional and helpful. The bike was shipped on a date agreed - 7working days after order. Good produce, great price, slow communication.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Excellent price, great customer service
review: Excellent price. The only slightly weird thing about this order was that the delivery company lost the package TWICE. Winstanleys were actually excellent at responding to me immediately and their customer service was excellent, so probably I should give 5 stars, it's just the delivery company was not good.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Competitive online retailer …
review: I’ve not use this online retailer before for any cycling stuff, but their ‘sale price’ for the item I was looking for, was the best out there. My order (for a pair of DMR V12 Pedals), came well-packaged and in its original sealed carton. As far as turnaround is concerned, I thought my order might have arrived a bit sooner than it did, as I placed my order on a Saturday and it showed up the following Thursday. But I’d have confidence in buying from Winstanleys again.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Quick delivery
review: Quick delivery. Also delivery with amazon so it was efficient.The picture on the website was not the exact picture of the item, this put me of from buying it because i could not compair. I only brought the item because I couldn't get it from another retailer that had the exact picture.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Bike needed more assembly than I anticipated.
review: Bike needed more assembly than I expected. Also more assembly than the qr code on the box showed. This included Wheel reflectors, front reflector, mud guard, handlebar, front wheel, brake line guards, pedals, bell - no instructions and still got a bolt, grommets and washers leftover which I don’t know what they were for. Took me a lot longer than the 15 mins that the qr code said as there was a lot more to do and it was fiddly. Came with a checklist to say how bike was tested but then it’s sent like this. Front wheel makes a noise like something is catching. Bought the same bike for my daughter elsewhere and that came fully assembled apart from turning the handlebar around and tightening four bolts.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Use a different courier
review: To be fair, the service from Winstanleys bikes was good. However the courier they chose to send the bike with was not. The courier, APC Network, left my bike outside my house, where it sat for 4 days as I was away. I was amazed as I had expected them not to deliver it without a signature given its obvious value as a new bike...

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Give your new bike a thorough check before deciding to keep it.
review: I paid £3000 for an Orro endurance bike. When it arrived I noticed slight damage to the front rim and a mark on the tyre which looked like someone had ridden it before. After calling their help center I was assured that no one had had it previously and they also refunded me £50. After riding the bike for a few weeks I seemed to struggle up hills that I had previously climbed easier on my previous machine.I checked the rear cassette size and noticed that the largest sprocket was 30 teeth instead of the 33 that was specified. A new cassette would cost in the region of £150 plus the possible cost of a flat top chain which was making the bike rather more expensive. I complained about this but was told that I could return the bike if it wasn't suitable. Due to the fact that I'd been riding it, I'm sure their returns policy wouldn't accept it. The reason for relating this experience is to warn those that purchase anything from Winstanley Bikes that they need to check everything thoroughly before accepting it.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: I had significant problems processing…
review: I had significant problems processing payment for order on laptop.  Tried many times without success and then worked first time on mobile phone.  Although only one order placed, payment was taken twice and I subsequently had to request refund which was given.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: It was the best price available BUT!
review: It was the best price available for the part I ordered and it was delivered promptly. However, Winstanley used Amazon delivery (not the Amazon shop as some ebayers do). I avoid Amazon at all costs as I dislike their business approach and attitude towards tax. This dissuades me from using Winstanley in the future as in some way I will be contributing to the Amazon machine.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Good Bike When Set Up Properly
review: Arrived quickly. Took me 3 hours of trying to get it set up before I gave up and took it to a bike shop. It needed the brakes adjusting, gears adjusting, front spokes tightening to bring the rim of the tyre in at certain points so that brakes didn’t catch. No point sending a tick sheet saying everything had been checked if it wasn’t ready to ride once the buyer puts on the handlebars, front wheel and pedals.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: New bike order
review: Website was misleading. Website stated dispatch after 1 day. Had order confirmation but no other info. After a week I rang and waited 25mins to speak to someone, for an update. Comms could have been better, everything else was fine. Bike was well packed and delivered in allocated hour time slot

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Bike was delivered in a box but damaged
review: Bike was delivered in a box. It seemed well protected and the frame was covered up in cardboard but the front disk break lever was broken. I have sent emails and pictures of the damage they acknowledged the damage and i am awaiting to see if they will replace the broken part or have me take the bike to a shop for repair. So the jury is still out on Winstanleys bikes to see how they perform for there customers.

review: I gave a lower score as I was promised next day delivery and it didn’t happen .I lost the computer for my electric bike on holiday and called to ask if they could send me one out next day (it was a Sunday)  I was advised to go on ebay first thing Monday morning and then call them with the order number.  My husband did this and volunteered extra payment for next day delivery - he as told that they would put it next day and no additional payment was required. We did not receive it next day which was disappointing.

The instructions are horrific really not easy to follow and so much is not relevant to actually building the bike. I’m awaiting a family member to review it before I feel confident to ride it. Worse than building ikea furniture. The company were good to deal with.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: The bike is still travelling
review: Ordered a cube aim pro on the 25/08/24 it said in stock at suppliers warehouse 7-8 days delivery. I waited the 8 days then called up after eventually getting through i was told it would be the 6th of September delivery would be expected. So i waited the 6th came and went with no update so i called again told they had had the date moved to the 13th expected delivery. Ok fair enough  it cant be helped. Waited till past the 13th and called again as id recieved no further update. When i got through was told that the expected date had changed again and would now be the 18th. Waited till past the 18th was told any day so waited another 5 days  on the 23rd i called and tried for over an hour to get through when i eventually did there was still no update so i asked for a refund which was processed. Unfortunately my experience of winstanleys bikes was not very good. 4 weeks of waiting to end up with a refund. Although not the company's fault as the delay was with supplier i feel the updates could of been better and possibly offered me a solution however no solution was offered so i had to get my bike from else where

title: Not overly impressed
review: Not overly impressed. I have ordered from these guys half a dozen times. Every time my order has taken ages to arrive. We're talking a week plus. OK fair enough. Postage is cheap. Royal mail isn't what it used to be. Blah blah, You can understand that. But I ordered 2 fork bags recently l and received an email 2 days later saying they don't have stock, and it would be over a month for delivery. I'm sorry, but that is not playing the game is it. No, would you like a refund? just, we'll send you the tracking number (if one is available) why are you selling items you clearly don't have. It's a piss take.

I understand that getting a bike from a manufacturer can be difficult but the customer support was appalling.

description: Established over 50 years ago, we are now one of Europes leading online bicycle retailers. We are driven to provide the best service possible and have maintained those traditional, customer focused values.
title: Only order if you are not in a hurry and don't mind waiting weeks for a delivery. Maybe... it might take even longer as I canceled my order.

After 10 days of waiting they then informed me that it wasn't going to be available from the supplier for maybe another 10 days. So this must mean that the above statement of it being in stock in the suppliers warehouse was false and they just want you to order it and then wait till they can get them.

Not your fault the driver was sooo late and just leaves it on the door step. Just change that and I’d give you a five star rating. It’s not a harsh rating, as it relates on your service.

title: Clean cars, terrible service
review: The company was communicative and the car was clean, and baby seat in perfect working order. The driver had a great understanding of installing the seat properly which is rare and appreciated, hence three stars instead of 2 or 1.The experience itself was poor. Our flight was delayed, and we provided our flight number and updates to the booking company. Other car transfer companies use this information to dispatch a car at an appropriate time relative to the delay. That was not the case here. The driver called me incessantly the second I landed saying he was already there. He started the one hour waiting clock before we had even taxied to the gate for an international flight. He called every 10-15 minutes from there asking for an update. The airline lost our bags (indeed, the entire flight’s bags) and this was not clear until we had waited for them for over 30 minutes. The entire time the driver kept calling asking what was going on, and asking us to abandon our bags.Eventually, we had to do so, which has resulted in huge delays in getting our bags back (our friends who waited it out were able to get theirs already). While leaving, he demanded we pay for his extended parking fee, even though he should not have come to the airport already, and had no reason to drive all the way to the parking area instead of a waiting lot. We paid it, at which point he demanded another 30 pounds for his waiting time (again, even though he had our flight information and should not have come so early. This type of behavior might be expected if we hired a single driver, but we booked with an agency expecting they would handle dispatch appropriately). He wanted to drive us to an ATM to get his cash, which I refused. Eventually, he had us give our credit card information over the phone. It was clear that a confrontation would ensue if we did not. Overall, the cars are clean, but the service is poor and predatory. I’d advise looking elsewhere.

I don’t want to go to a chain like Halfords so thought I would try here but it was pointless I’ll be going to Halfords next time, and the tyres I originally picked and ordered where out of stock so they’ve put different ones on. title: Delivery charge / return charge too expensive

After already paying £5.99 delivery on top of a £200 order which was a shock in itself as most companies offer free delivery over at least £50 I then had to pay £6 to return the pair of boots that was too big. Usually most companies now offer free delivery then a free return so for £12 each time I think I will be ordering off many of the other competitive sites. Little disappointed!

title: HUNT Trail Wide MTB 29 Wheelset - 29"
review: I'm not much for leaving reviews normally...however.  After my first ride on the new wheels I was very very pleased with the quality, strength and stability of this wheelset.  I upgraded the stock wheels on my Intense 951 Carbon Fiber XC bike.  Huge improvement, noticeable immediately. I spoke with a tech at Hunt who was patient and walked me through everything needed to purchase the correct set.  I had a problem with the hub and they remedied a solution quickly and efficiently.  Very happy with my purchase - the people and the product are terrific.

title: Your bike called, it wants these wheels.
review: First off, I made a mistake when ordering. I ordered boost spacing when I needed non boost spacing and when I entered my axle spacing as non boost the team noticed and reached out. It was a simple fix and my wheels arrived timely. Service at Hunt was excellent! Tires mounted easily, so the tape was secure and the valves seem to be great, I love the built in valve core removal tool. Riding these wheels made a massive difference! My wheels weighed 1732g (kitchen scale, tags on) without valves, which was just over a pound lower than my previous set. Hub engagement is smooth and quick, but not lightning fast. However, technical riding is easily managed even through steep, rocky, chunk. For me, one of the biggest selling points was availability of non boost spacing. It's hard to find modern, quality wheels with QR hubs but the real MVP here is price; a complete wheel set for the price of one normal rear wheel? Yes please! If you're looking for an affordable set of wheels that are built to run mile after mile from a company that prioritizes customer service, check out Hunt. Your wallet and Strava PRs will thank you!

title: Wheel overall are great, tubeless tape job was subpar on one wheel.
review: Order, tracking, delivery, wheel quality and ride performance is top notch. Really enjoying them. Only issue was the tubeless tape job on front wheel was subpar. Noticed that front wasn't as smooth as back but didn't think much of it. Mounted tires and soon realized front wheel/tire lost air quickly (including through spoke holes). Rear was great. Dismounted front tire and found several locations tape was creased and was allowing air and sealant to escape to valve and spoke holes. Pulled the factory tape, cleaned and reinstalled new tubeless tape. Front wheel has been flawless since then.

title: It was my first purchase from Hunt and…
review: It was my first purchase from Hunt and it was to forget, a very bad experience, with a first pair arriving with a terrible finish on one of the rims, which I initially thought was a "scratch or crack", I contacted SAC, which worked well taking care of the shipping label for returns.The problem was that on the second pair of wheels that arrived to me, the problem persisted and to make matters worse, one of the rim tapes was completely loose, which I had to change to be able to use the tubeless tire, one of the spokes had a loose pint, where the support to the The client told me to correct it with a permanent paint pen and that they apologized for what happened, as it wasn't a rule they worked like that, but what is certain is that the finish on the wheels is very bad, be it the paint or varnish, it's terrible, I don't know. If I had bought the pair of wheels on sale and they already knew about the aesthetic defects of the rims, I would have preferred if Hunt had told me that the price was lower due to the defects.P.S- The offer of a cycling cap doesn't solve everything

title: HUNT 50 Carbon Wide Aero…
review: I bought a HUNT 50 Carbon Wide Aero wheelset in June last year. They are quick but I used them once a week for about 10 months (maybe 5 or 6 times in the wet) before I needed to replace the freehub bearings and one wheel bearing (only guaranteed for 6 months). I was always very careful when washing and made sure that solvents didn't go anywhere near the freehub and wheel bearings. The rear wheel also needed trueing but a lot of the spoke nipples were seized so I needed a complete wheel rebuild. I have been riding for 50 years but never needed to replace any wheel/freehub bearings until now.

title: Good looking wheels poorly built and badly supported
review: The freehub that was installed on the wheel initially must have been really soft as a piece came off when I installed the cassette which meant that the retaining ring didn't take. Hunt sent me a new freehub and this was installed successfully. However, once I got the bike out on a ride, it was apparent pretty quickly that there was too much flex in the wheels and once I got out of the saddle (sprinting or climbing) the wheels rubbed against the frame. It has been nearly three weeks since this was raised with Hunt and they haven't got back to me about remedying the situation. Good marketing, nice looking design, really poor customer experience.

review: I received a wheelset that had several scrapes and blemishes on the rim. The process to return the wheels was relatively smooth and there was continuous dialogue with customer service.

title: Cube Attain
review: Well the delivery was fast and efficient, the bike arriving within a couple of days of the order. It's a nice looking although I'm not mad about the bright orange handlebar tape. The first negative is the cables. There's virtually no play. I was going to raise the handlebars slightly but that's certainly not possible. It really needs a couple of extra inches in each of the cables running down from the handlebars. It took a while before I was able to get out on the bike but now I've had the chance and I'm disappointed. Within 15 miles I had a puncture. The tyres, Continental Ultrasport, are utter rubbish. They're wafer thin. No where near what's required for British roads, even in the summer. Ok they cost a bit more, but Continental Gatorskins should have been used. Why not put Gatorskins on? I don't get it.The disk brakes are good, but they're going to need a bit of adjustment to get them right. The gears, again need a bit of adjustment to get the links to sit squarely on the sprockets.So overall the bike's OK, but I'm now going to have to spend an extra £80 on a decent set of tyres.

title: Good+poor=average
review: There were good areas and some which I think could be improved on. So spent just over £3000 on a Cube Electric mountain bike. I decided to purchase it after a fairly detailed discussion with one of the staff who was pretty informative. It arrived within a couple of days and was well packaged I duly unpacked it and followed the link to the youtube video that showed me how to assemble it or so I thought. The chap on the video pulled out the bike with all the handlebar attachments already on such as gears brakes, seat post and monitor so all he had to do was to attach the bars but mine had had all the bar components detached so I didnt know what went where and the video didnt really show it. All there was appeared to be a piece of paper explaining that the parts were now not put on the bar because they could be stretched in transit, the diagram was generic and very simplified. So fair enough if the company can't fit the bar parts but it was poor that there was little in the way of any instruction of what goes where. However, next day I contacted Pauls and Adam was very helpful indeed and sent me a video of a bike like mine they had assembled that day so that was fine, but something like this needs go out with the bike so that the customer has something to go by. I managed to complete the assembly of the bike reasonably easily and then wanted to go on to how the electronic display works and in general how the bike operates but all that was sent was again a generic manual and a leaflet with a reference to user manuals being online (but no link provided) and that there are also apps but again no links or description of how they would help. All in all, the delivery was fine, information as to assembly was poor until Adam sent me his video which was excellent. Information as to things that would help me in my first few days with the bike was poor and this included links to a specific manual and relevants apps I could use. I ended up having to ring a mate who had a Cube 140 and getting info such as links and apps that would help.

title: Request bike in original packaging to avoid poor assembly issues.
review: I ordered a 20-inch wheel bike from Paul Cycles and was shocked by its condition upon arrival. For a brand-new bike, it had several issues that should have been caught if the bike had been properly assembled and inspected by experts. Here’s what I encountered:- Rear brake rotor rubbing on brake pads.- Brake levers not adjusted for children’s hands, levers set at the furthest from handlebar setting.- Scratches on both the crank and derailleur.- The derailleur protector, meant to prevent transit damage, was tossed loosely in the box with random paper.- Gears were not indexed correctly.- Grease was smeared over the seat clamp (where it shouldn’t be), and almost no grease was applied where it was necessary, like the seatpost.- Rear brake caliper arrived scratched.- The front brake pad transport spacer was missing, causing the brake pads to sit too close together.- The "Important Please Read" card was placed upside down, indicating a lack of care during assembly.When I initially emailed to address these issues, I received no response, and only after a week and a follow-up phone call did they reply. Their only solution was to offer a refund, which wasn’t helpful as I wanted to keep the bike for my son’s Christmas gift (and now it’s out of stock).I would’ve given a 1-star rating, but they did at least attempt to resolve the issue with a refund. However, a refund doesn’t address the larger problem of quality control in their assembly process. For anyone considering purchasing from them, I’d recommend requesting the bike in its original packaging or having a trusted mechanic assemble it to avoid the hassle I went through.

title: Bought a XR 5.9 from Paul's Cycles back…
review: Bought a XR 5.9 from Paul's Cycles back in March. It's done around 300 miles now mostly in dry conditions and the rear wheel bearings seem to have gone. I've contacted Paul's who have offered a £25 'goodwill' gesture towards the repair (4 bearings in rear wheel and freewheel) because apparently bearings only have a 90 day guarantee, something ive not even heard of before - suppose it sums up the quality if thats all they give. also contacted Lapierre's UK distributor who couldn't even be bothered and referred me back to Paul's. For wheel bearings to go so soon is nothing I've heard of before. Suggesting it's a "serviceable item" as if thats normal or fine for it to happen in this time and use frame is nonsense. There also seems to be issues with a rear suspension pivot constantly loosening itself off and much cracking from the rear suspension despite everything repeatedly being torqued up.All in all not a quality product and one to avoid.

description:
Having bought over 3.5 million cars and vans, webuyanycar has quickly become the nation’s favourite online car buying service. We provide a quick, simple and incredibly convenient alternative to the time-intensive traditional methods of selling your car or van. From our free 30-second online car valuation, to our 500+ UK branches, every step of the webuyanycar process defines simplicity and convenience. 

And don't forget... we also buy vans! Just head to www.webuyanyvan.com for your free van valuation.

Here’s how quick and easy it is to sell your car or van with webuyanycar.


•	Online Car Valuation


Finding out how much your car is worth couldn’t be easier. Simply enter your car’s reg number on our website, followed by a few simple details such as the vehicle’s mileage, the number of previous owners the car has had and the amount of service history you have on the car, and you’ll receive a free and instant online car valuation. Our valuations are closely monitored and adjusted according to market value trends as well as the condition and history of your vehicle. If you’re happy with the online car valuation you receive, you can easily move on to the next step of the car selling process.


•	Book an Appointment


If you’re happy with your valuation and are interested in selling your car, we have over 450 branches across the UK, providing a local branch to almost every major town and city.  In fact, we now have that many branches in the UK that the average time to your local webuyanycar location is just 13 minutes from anywhere in the country! Simply move on to the appointment calendar page, and book a slot at a time and location that is convenient for you.


•	Sell Your Car


At your appointment, you’ll meet one of our friendly branch managers who will take you through the car selling process and give your vehicle a quick inspection to ensure the condition matches up with that stated in your online car valuation. From there, we’ll head back inside to quickly go through the simple paperwork, and if you’re happy to sell you can choose to do so there and then! In fact, you could value your car, book and attend an appointment and sell your car in under an hour if you wished to; it’s that simple!
Value and sell your car the quick and easy way, with webuyanycar.

title: Unfair deductions made
review: On reflection the deductions made on the price seem unreasonable. When I explained this to the person her sugggested that even if I had got it repaired, I would have had similar reductions made to price quoted as on their spreadsheet it’s points for any repair work. I felt overwhelmed and ended up accepting a quote which, when discussed with experts 1hr later seem h reasonable.

title: My Brompton T Line is marvellous
review: My Brompton T Line is marvellous.  I am very happy with it. Mostly !  1. One reservation, that has to do with quality control at the factory and before delivery.  The gear cable was touching the chainwheel, because it had not been secured in the housing / little rectangle holder where the brake cable is also secured.  Just a little thing.  Small details count.  I have just secured it to the brake cable with a cable tie which will do until I get around to rerouting the gear cable. 2. Second, my Brompton toolkit will now not fit in the new oversize Ti tubing.  Why ?  Surely this could have been foreseen and a plastic holder or something that does fit could have been foreseen / invented so that we could continue to put our Brompton toolkit in the frame, as before.  Again, small thing, but it would have made me happy to be able to continue carrying my Brompton toolkit (over £60 to buy !) 3. Third, I get that Brompton is trying to make this bike as lightweight as possible, so they use Tubolito inner tubes, £25 a pop.  I had a puncture within a few days using these lightweight Tubolito and the Schwalbe One tyres the bike came with.  Usually, I throw away a punctured inner tube and put in a new one, but not at £25 a pop !  So, now I've got myself some conventional inner tubes - £6 - and will endure just that little bit of extra weight, rather than having to fix Tubolito inner tubes, or throw them away and waste £25.  Happy riding !

title: The new G-line
review: Ordered with a cyclescheme voucher, was delivered within 48 hours. As a long time Brompton user, the G-line was a leap of faith. My last P-line is slick, small, lightweight and travels well. The G-line is bigger, and heavier, and takes a bit of use in manouvering when folded. This bike won't be for the stallwart Brompton fans, but I have to say, its EVERYTHING I've ever wanted a bike to be. From the bigger wheels, the bold look, the ride position, the new fold clips, the super slick 8 speed hub, its the most fun I've had on a Brompton in 20 years of riding them (I think I've had 6 over the years - ive still got 3!). If small and simple is what you're after, the G line is not for you - this is a more tactical machine. Size has not compromised speed or function though - its fast, and responsive, and I think it will last me on much longer multi terrain rides rather than just the commute to work. A clear step away from the standard Brompton 16" wheel and form factor, but its incredibly well designed and executed, with refinements from the original. Choose wisely and decisively, and you won't be let down... Love it !

The new bracket looks great, and everything has been handled excellently.However, I did notice a couple of small areas that could be improved. There was some excess oil on the bike, which I believe wasn’t applied by your team, but it could have been wiped off. Additionally, I noticed some rust on parts inside the tube, which could have been cleaned as well. Also, the luggage block seemed to cause some wobbling, but other than that, I couldn’t find any other issues.Overall, I’d rate the service a solid 4.2/5. It’s one of the best services I’ve had, much better than some Brompton dealers I’ve encountered who didn’t seem to fully understand how the bike works. Kudos to your team for the amazing job—they truly did a great job!Thank you again for the excellent service, and I look forward to continuing to ride my Brompton!Best regards,Chun

title: Etyre can’t tell when tyre can be delivered, and kept us waiting for 2.5 hours
review: Etyre compared to other website is £40 cheaper for fun flat tyre I was looking for. They did offer 24 hour fitting and I can choose a time slot for fitting at the fitter. After confirmed for me for the 8:30 slot next morning, I turned up on time for appointment with my run flat tyre, which means I have no spare car and I can only drive the flat tyre for 50 miles. Been told by fitter that tyre was not delivered. And they were not been informed when it will be sent. We don’t have any notice to mention late delivery neither. Called eTyre, the lady on the phone said the driver was out for delivery, she can’t narrow the time down for us, but it should be delivered before 12pm. She did offer refund but it’s pointless for us to accept a refund as we do need tyre to be fitted that day! The uncertainty about when tyre can be delivered also means we have to cancel the train we booked at 11:39, and we can’t do anything apart from wandering around for hours waiting for the driver. After waiting for 2 hours we called again, the lady told us no more update but same message driver will be with us before 12.Finally the tyre was delivered 2.5 hours after our appointment time. The system for appointment between client and fitter isn’t aligned with the delivery system of etyre. They should notice both fitter and client if they can’t deliver the tyre before the appointment time. The appointment slot is pointless if nobody knows exactly when tyre will be sent to fitter, it’s totally waste of client’s time too! Suggest to improve the logistic transparency if etyre is proud of quick service within 24 hours and offers precise appointment time. Royal Mail and Amazon can do it, you can also do it! Until this happens, we won’t use it again just to save £40 but have to drive 40 mins and wait 2.5 hours.m, cancel train ticket …

title: delays in ETYRES processes
review: Before 9am one day, I ordered & paid for 2 Bridgestone all-season front tyres (and wheel alignment), online - slick website experience, thus far.  Middle of the afternoon, I received an email saying that they wouldn't be able to get the tyres to the fitter until a couple of days later than the appointed date/time.  Via email ('cause etyres claimed they couldn't get thru to my mobile number - they seem to be only ones having any difficulties), we set a new appointment for Just Tyres to do their work. I turned up at the local JustTyres, in good time, for the agreed appointment.  I discussed why I was there, and then was sitting happily in the customer waiting room while the work was being undertaken. Some time elapsed and then I was told that only 1 of the 2 tyres ordered, had been delivered, and (weird or what?) that JustTyres had fitted the one new tyre; I was offered the option of getting JustTyres to order (with me paying for, doubtless at a higher cost) the missing tyre off them (they had none in stock, of course), or, for me to contact ETyres.  I rang etyres, was told I was in a queue with an expected wait time of 5 minutes.  About 25 minutes later, I got speaking to their phone-person, who apologised for the situation, and said he would chase it up and get back to me.  I said that this was poor service and wanted to know how he would recompense me for the appalling service - he said he would not be doing that, as they do not do that.  I said that I wanted to hear that day as to what the situation was.  I emailed them at about 5.30pm that day, for an update and to re-express my dissatisfaction; I repeated similar emails twice the next day, and still I have heard nothing.  ETyres treat customers very badly - their idea of what good customer service looks like is extremely poor.  How a company reacts to things going wrong at their end, is the measure of a good company, and ETYRES COMES UP VERY SHORT (they should look towards the likes of John Lewis or Amazon, for great customer service).  ETYRES are great at taking a customer's money, BUT AFTER GETTING THAT CASH, watch out.   I still wait to discover how and when they will fulfill the contract, and what, if anything, they might offer me to help turn around my views on them.9.1.23 I attended a further appointment to discover, yet again, that the missing tyre had not turned up, and then at a further appointment after that, at last, the tyre was there, and got fitted.  Having kept ETyres abreast of their failings, they agreed to send me a £20 Amazon voucher as a gesture of goodwill.  I accepted that.

title: Good enough work, excessive wait time.
review: Good work, but just LOTS of waiting on the day. A little bit nervously ordered my tyres online (what if they don't fit?) - initially just rear tyres and booked a date and time - a Tuesday at 10.45am. After getting my car serviced elsewhere, I was recommended to get the front tyres replaced as well, due tracking wear on one side. I couldn't add this on to the original appointment (a bit annoying after phoning them specifically to ask) but had to book it as a second job. LUCKILY I managed to book the very next slot after 10.45am - so in theory, all good. On the day, I turned up 10mins early to be told they only had 2 tyres delivered, sorry! Will have to come back again. Not pleased, so they double-checked and after a hunt around they found the other 2. Phew, back on track! .....and I know I've booked the next 2 slots so this should be a doddle..... not a waste of my time. But no, they were already running one hour late (and all of this by just 10.45am in the morning). So, I was told to come back by 12.30 and it would all be done for sure. Came back at 12.30 and it wasn't done for sure!Finished at 1pm - due in work by 2pm - so all quite stressful in the end.As a summary then, it is a little nerve racking buying your tyres online when it will (to some extent) rely on your own ability to read off the many numbers on the side of your existing tyres. The booking-in system makes you feel like things will run to time on the day  - but no, its just as bad as in the old days i.e. turn up and hang around for 2 and half hours. If you think Dr's appointment, you'll be mentally prepared:)

title: Management Needs Improvement

The guy in the morning at reception was friendly as usual, but by the time I came to pick up the car at 5 pm the manager was different .  (Also they said I needed wheel alignment , after doing the same thing a few months prior) - but I’ll take their word for it . And then the manager confused my Audi A1 with an Audi Q3 and charged me for the latter , brought out the wrong invoice and car and when I corrected him he made me feel it was my fault.I could have literally driven off with someone else’s car . You should always ask for some sort of ID or address details before handing over a car- the guy also made a sarcastic comment to me for not noticing it earlier .  Didn’t apologise , almost acted like it was my fault  and then refunded me and sent me on my way , was okay in the end but customer service this time was  seriously lacking , normally it is much better but that was a different manager . They didn’t even tell me the service was done, I went down at 5 pm and asked myself . The guys doing the actual work are pretty good , have had a good experience with them each time . The work is solid but the management, at least with this particular manager needs to improve ,this particular manager / receptionist wearing a bandana seemed to have lost all desire to live , seems like he doesn’t care about himself , customers or the world . Looks incredibly unhappy -  In which case I would recommend doing something else .

The car failed its MOT but I found another garage who were able to repair the faults and retest it for at least £200 less than Formula 1 were quoting. title: Average for OEM quality but acceptable
review: This is going to be a short but simple review. I'll put some photos on my blog for comparison/further review and a follow up for later date.I don't consider these the best quality car mats you can buy, but for "OEM" supplied quality they are acceptable to use, and an acceptable price including delivery so would deal with again. The negatives first, this isn't a reflection on the company, just my experience with my orderCommunication. There wasn't much of it, emails did warn they were running with minimal staff, but the reviews on here suggest it's hit and miss. I ended up receiving my order through a different courier and had to chase customer service to get a response. I was actually worried these were dropshippers or scammers due to the lack of comms, but figured they were a legit business after reading the number of reviews they had. They arrived about 6 days after orderingQuality of fit. The mats are advertised as OEM quality. To me this means exactly as it would come from the manufacturer, so no modification or hassle to fit. In terms of fitting, YES, the mats fit (Audi A3 Sportback 2007). However I had to give a little nudge here and there and bend the mats over the pop on fitments. If you buy them for the same car as me, I'd recommend fitting the pop on section nearest the handbrake first as the mat curves upwards slightly if you don't and doesn't push on properlyThe mats themselves were slightly oversized and stiff, they may loosen over time  as they take shape because they're new. Or this could simply be by design to add a little extra protection.This wouldn't deter me from ordering again however, because they were of a good enough standard and a vast improvement over the non-OEM mats that the car seller had thrown into my car. The push on connectors were the right size and give a reliable feel when pushing on too so they're nice and tightSide note: you might want to change the colour of the sticker stitch on the tag on the mat. I find the blue to be hard to read. Maybe something like white or red would stand out more (white probably) as bright text on dark backgrounds helps to focus the reader

title: Please make sure you open all parts in 24 hours
review: I had previously had no problems with Paddocks, and their prices and postage are reasonable and fast (Australia). I have purchased thousands of dollars worth of products for my Series Land Rovers. I recently contacted them about a missing part from a full hood set for my Series 2A 63, but I was told you only have 24 hours to inform them of a missing part. They showed no insight into how restorations work, how long they take, and how putting on a hood set and canvas are the last things you do. Given my customer history, I would have thought they would have been generous and just said, "Yep, let's work this out." Anyway, I had to sort it out myself, but I'll only ever use Paddocks as a last resort now, so while they saved money at my expense, they will undoubtedly lose more over the coming years.
